newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans, soy products limit up on USDA data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans, soy products limit up on USDA data.

text.p: CBOT soybeans opened up the daily 30-cent-per-bushel trading limit Friday on bullish ending stocks and production data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, traders said.
Both soyoil and soymeal futures also opened limit up, keying off strength from soybean futures, traders said.
USDA put the final 1996 U.S. soybean crop production estimate at 2.382 billion bushels. That figure was lower than trade expectations and lower than USDA's previous estimate of 2.403 billion bushels.
Traders also said the government decision to lower the soybean carryout to 155 million bushels from a previous estimate of 180 million was also bullish.

At 0938 CST, CBOT soybeans were 30 cents per bushel higher, with January up 34-1/2 at $7.30. Soyoil was 0.98 to 1.00 cent per lb higher, with March up 1.00 at 24.76. Soymeal was $9.30 to $10.50 per ton, with March up $10.00 at $230.10.
January contracts are in the delivery period and trade without limits, according to CBOT regulations.
